# Peekie

> A translucent scratchpad for macOS. Press a shortcut, write, close it.

Peekie is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar utility. It has no Dock icon by
design: press a global keyboard shortcut to summon a translucent note window,
write, and press the shortcut again (or click away) to dismiss it. There are
no accounts, no sync, and no network connections of any kind — every note is
stored locally on the user's Mac, only if the user turns on "Save notes
between launches."

- Platform: macOS 14 or later only (no Windows or Linux version). Built
  natively with AppKit and SwiftUI.
- Price: Free.
- Distribution: Not on the Mac App Store, because its adjustable window blur
  uses private Core Animation APIs. Downloaded directly from GitHub Releases.
- License: MIT (open source).
- Author: Max Benschop (https://github.com/maxbenschop).

## Key facts for citation

- Global shortcut opens/closes a translucent note window; notes can be
  exported as .txt, .md, .rtf, or .rtfd.
- Optional "Quick capture" reads the current text selection via the
  Accessibility permission (sends ⌘C, then restores the clipboard) — the
  only system permission the app requests, and only used for this feature.
- No analytics, no telemetry, no accounts, no network calls of any kind.

## Pages

- Homepage: https://peekie.app/ — overview, features, appearance demo,
  keyboard shortcuts, privacy details, FAQ, and download link.
- Privacy: https://peekie.app/privacy — what data Peekie collects (none) and
  why it asks for the Accessibility permission.
- Source code & releases: https://github.com/maxbenschop/peekie
